# Agent operating protocol (shared by all project agents)

This file is mandatory reading for every project agent in `.claude/agents/`. It condenses section 0 of `docs/source/master-prompt-v2.0.md`. Where they differ, the master prompt wins.

## Two gate systems: never mix them

- **DG0–DG7** are *software delivery gates* for the engineering team. Their records live in `docs/delivery/`.
- **G1–G6** are *business transformation approvals inside the product* (Case for Change … Sustain). They are product features.
- An engineering agent can never grant a real business, Finance or IT production approval. A demo Sponsor approval in seed data approves nothing real.
- Product gate G6 (Sustain) never implies that engineering gate DG7 has passed, and DG7 never implies any G1–G6 business approval.

## Sources of truth

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Authoritative methodology (playbook v1.0) | `docs/source/playbook.md` (block anchors `B0001`–`B0165`); original `docs/source/Business_Transformation_Playbook.docx` |
| Product and delivery requirements | `docs/source/master-prompt-v2.0.md` (sections §0–§21) |
| Requirement register | `docs/delivery/requirements.csv` |
| Stage state and candidates | `docs/delivery/stages.json`, `docs/delivery/candidates/` |
| Decisions and assumptions | `docs/delivery/decisions.md` |
| Findings | `docs/delivery/findings.json` |
| Reviews / gates | `docs/delivery/reviews/DGx/round-N/`, `docs/delivery/gates/DGx.json` |
| Gate rules (validator) | `tools/gates/` (implementers must not edit it) |

## Assignment contract (what every delegation contains)

Every assignment names: stage ID; task and requirement IDs; exact source/reference files; candidate/base revision; permitted files; constraints; input/output contracts; acceptance checks; dependency status; and the expected handback path. If any of these is missing or contradictory, say so in your handback. Do not guess.

Verify the starting revision (`git rev-parse HEAD`, and `git status`) before you write anything. Do not assume your workspace contains the latest integration candidate.

## Implementation handback contract

Write your handback to the path given in the assignment (default `docs/delivery/handbacks/<stage>/<task-id>-<role>.md`). It must contain:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# qa-verifier DG7 round 4 (T-DG7-REV-QA-R4): A18 on a fresh archive built from the FROZEN candidate clone (471072d6).
# Part 1: transfer-drill.sh directly with --keep, so the target cluster's pg.log shows whether D9 really stopped and
#         restarted PostgreSQL (F-DG7-921, independent of the register's citation).
# Part 2: the shipped A18 harness (tests/qa/integration/a18-transfer-drill.test.ts) with QA_A18_REQUIRE=1 on the same
#         archive (missing inputs FAIL, never skip).
# Run under tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh. SYNTHETIC data only; nothing here approves anything (no G1-G6, Finance, IT, DG).
set -u
REPO="${QA_REPO:?}"; OUT="${QA_OUT:?}"; B="$TMPDIR/qa-r4-a18"; CAND=sha256:d91f7152950ed7119b412db0135836c53a3f01e95300af32c86db367f0712e59
[ -e "$B" ] && { echo "BLOCKED: $B exists"; exit 2; }
cd "$REPO"; ts() { date -u +%T; }
echo "start $(ts); HEAD $(git rev-parse HEAD); node $(node -v); free $(df -Pm "$TMPDIR" | awk 'NR==2{print $4}') MB"
U=$(node -e 'const u=new URL(process.env.TEST_DATABASE_ADMIN_URL);u.pathname="/mth_a18_src";u.username="mth_owner";console.log(u.href)')
psql -X -q -d "$TEST_DATABASE_ADMIN_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 <<SQL
DO \$\$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname='mth_owner') THEN CREATE ROLE mth_owner LOGIN; END IF;
IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname='mth_app') THEN CREATE ROLE mth_app LOGIN; END IF; END \$\$;
CREATE DATABASE mth_a18_src OWNER mth_owner ENCODING 'UTF8' TEMPLATE template0;
GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE mth_a18_src TO mth_app;
SQL
(cd packages/db && DATABASE_OWNER_URL="$U" NODE_ENV=development node --conditions=@mth/source src/cli.ts migrate >/dev/null && \
  DATABASE_OWNER_URL="$U" NODE_ENV=development node --conditions=@mth/source src/cli.ts seed-demo | grep "reporting periods relative to") || { echo "demo db FAIL"; exit 1; }
DATABASE_OWNER_URL="$U" NODE_ENV=development node tools/migration/export.mjs --out "$B/export" --operator "transfer-drill synthetic operator" | tail -3
echo "demo export exit ${PIPESTATUS[0]}; manifest sha256 $(sha256sum "$B/export/manifest.json" | cut -c1-64)"
node tools/release/build-archive.mjs --repo "$REPO" --commit "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" --demo-data "$B/export" --candidate $CAND --out "$B/arch" | tail -3
echo "build-archive exit ${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
A=$(ls "$B"/arch/*.tar.gz | head -1); S=$(sha256sum "$A" | cut -c1-64); echo "archive $(basename "$A") $(stat -c %s "$A") bytes sha256 $S"
node tools/release/build-archive.mjs --verify "$A" --expect-sha256 "$S" --candidate $CAND; echo "archive --verify exit $?"
psql -X -q -d "$TEST_DATABASE_ADMIN_URL" -c "DROP DATABASE mth_a18_src WITH (FORCE);"; rm -rf "$B/export"
mkdir -p "$B/store" && cp -a "${QA_STORE_SRC:?}" "$B/store/v10"
mkdir -p "$OUT/direct"; W="$B/work"
echo "--- part 1: transfer-drill.sh --keep start $(ts) free $(df -Pm "$TMPDIR" | awk 'NR==2{print $4}') MB"
bash deploy/scripts/transfer-drill.sh --archive "$A" --sha256 "$S" --store "$B/store" --out "$OUT/direct" --work "$W" --keep > "$OUT/direct/stdout.txt" 2> "$OUT/direct/stderr.txt"
rc1=$?; echo "part 1 drill exit $rc1 $(ts)"; grep -E '^transfer-drill: (step D[0-9]+ (PASS|FAIL)|PASS|FAIL)' "$OUT/direct/stdout.txt"
echo "stderr lines: $(wc -l < "$OUT/direct/stderr.txt")"; head -5 "$OUT/direct/stderr.txt"
echo "--- target cluster pg.log: shutdown / startup lines (F-DG7-921)"
grep -n -E 'received fast shutdown|database system is shut down|database system is ready to accept connections|starting PostgreSQL' "$W/pgT/pg.log" | sed 's/^/  /'
cp "$W/pgT/pg.log" "$OUT/direct/pgT-pg.log" 2>/dev/null
pgrep -f "$W/pg" >/dev/null && echo "drill PostgreSQL left running: YES" || echo "drill PostgreSQL left running: none"
rm -rf "$W"; echo "removed work tree $(ts)"
echo "--- part 2: A18 harness start $(ts) free $(df -Pm "$TMPDIR" | awk 'NR==2{print $4}') MB"
mkdir -p "$OUT/harness"
QA_A18_REQUIRE=1 QA_A18_ARCHIVE="$A" QA_A18_ARCHIVE_SHA256="$S" QA_A18_STORE="$B/store" QA_A18_OUT="$OUT/harness" \
  npx vitest run --project integration tests/qa/integration/a18-transfer-drill.test.ts --reporter=verbose
rc2=$?; echo "A18 harness exit $rc2 end $(ts)"
rm -rf "$B"; echo "removed $B"
echo "part 1 drill exit $rc1; part 2 harness exit $rc2"
[ "$rc1" -eq 0 ] && [ "$rc2" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
exit 0

**Tests:**

| Test | Proves |
| --- | --- |
| T-B15 | `allowance.mjs` writes a `/3` file that `parseAllowance` accepts. A counter table appears only in `counters`. |
| T-B17 (PostgreSQL) | As in B.7, on the **full** A3.6 chain (C0–C6): the journey reaches `decideGate` 201, and the changed tables minus `tables`, operational and `user_identity` equal `D8_TOUCHED_AUDITED ∪ D8_TOUCHED_CHILDREN ∪ D8_TOUCHED_COUNTERS`. Mode 2 with the generated `/3` file exits 0, and the report's `automationChain` is non-empty. The negative case of B.7 stays. |
| T-B18 (PostgreSQL) | The remedy table is closed: on a fixture where the chosen gate misses a code with no remedy row, the journey stops at C1 with `D8 FAIL: no API remedy for <code> at <pointer>` and writes nothing after it |
| T-B11 | As in B.6 DO-D2 and B.7: D0–D11 PASS in the no-network namespace, on an archive built from the merged candidate commit. `reconcile-d5.json` and `reconcile-d6.json` are `matched`, with an `audit_already_present` delta. `reconcile-d9.json` is `matched after use`. The report's `result` is `PASS`. |

**What DO-D4 must know.**
- A row that mode 2 calls unexplained is reported with its key, never allowed by editing the lists by hand. The lists come from T-B17's measurement only.
- A scheduled automation row that lands in the window (A3.9 residual 1) is a FAIL with its key and trigger code. Never pause, disable or reschedule a job to avoid it. Report it, and the orchestrator decides.
- `table-digest` output may be piped again once BE-R3's drain fix is merged. The file-based workaround of DO-D3 may stay.
- Wait at least 30 s after C6 (and after the gate routing in C4) before D9's snapshot, and record the wait. A worker job that ends later than that is a T-B17 measurement gap, reported as such.
- Every IdP user, secret, origin, KPI value, evidence note, deferral and gate decision is SYNTHETIC. Nothing here approves anything: no G1–G6, Finance or IT approval, and no DG gate.
- Disk is tight. Measure first, never make a second full checkout, and delete the work tree unless `--keep` is given.
- Run before the handback: `node tools/gates/validate.mjs --historical --stage DG6` **first**; then the drill tests under `with-pg.sh`, T-B11, `pnpm -r typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm openapi:lint` and the repository-wide prettier check.

### B.9 DO-D7: run T-B11 and the A18 harness to the end (devops-engineer; repair; after BE-R4)

65:5. **D9 job checks are not built.** The checks for pg-boss rows, `job_run`, enabled `job_schedule` equality, and a job queued before the stop completing after it, are missing.

  D-260's escalation condition is "Amendment 3 needs to loosen the allowance beyond what the drill's journal explains". A3.8 shows that it is **not** met. A3.9 names the one case that would meet it (scheduled automation) and keeps that case unexplained.
- **Two gate systems.** Nothing in this amendment grants or implies a G1–G6, Finance or IT approval, and nothing reads or writes DG0–DG7. Every D8 write, including the G5 submission and its decision, is SYNTHETIC drill data on a disposable target. It approves nothing real.

### A3.1 Automation rows: the facts that decide it

The facts below were read in the code at the base revision.

- **The measured row comes from a seeded starter.** It is not an ADMIN rule. `starter.transformation_created` (0075) has `run_as = 'service'`. The starter wrapper (`apps/worker/src/automation/starters.ts`, l.212) writes `initiating_user_id: null`. CHECK `automation_execution_identity` makes `initiating_user_id` non-NULL only for `run_as = 'initiating_user'`. **So for the row DO-D3 measured, `initiating_user_id` is NULL.** A rule over `initiating_user_id` alone, as D-260 worded it, would not explain it. The G5 chain (A3.6) adds `gate.submitted` and `gate.decided` starters, whose catalogue `initiating_user_field` is NULL as well.
- **The trigger link is recorded, immutably.**
  - `automation_execution.trigger_key` is the envelope's `idempotencyKey`, and `trigger_code` is its `eventType` (`starters.ts` l.126–138, `engine.ts`).
  - The relay copies `idempotencyKey` from `outbox_event.idempotency_key` (`apps/worker/src/relay.ts` l.78).
  - `automation_execution_guard` (0074) refuses any later change of `trigger_code`, `trigger_key`, `trigger_payload`, `run_as` and `initiating_user_id`.
- **The outbox row is written in the transaction of the mutation that raised it.** Examples:
  - `createTransformation` writes aggregate `transformation` (`routes.ts` l.298);
  - `submitGate` and `decideGate` write aggregate `gate_instance` (`gates.ts` `enqueueGateEvent`).

  `outbox_event.created_at` and `audit_event.occurred_at` both default to `now()`, PostgreSQL's transaction timestamp. Neither insert path sets them (`packages/db/src/audit.ts`, `apps/api/src/modules/jobs/outbox.ts`, `gates.ts`). So the mutation's audit event and its outbox row carry the **same** timestamp.
- **The worker's own writes carry the job.** Every worker audit event has `request_id = 'job:<pg-boss job id>'` (`jobActor`). A starter wrapper and the handler it wraps run in the same job, so they write under the same `request_id`. The engine (queue `automation.evaluate`) writes its executions and their actions' effects in its own job, again under one `request_id`. That includes the execution, the action result and the handler's outputs, such as a gate routing's approval rows.
- **`outbox_event` is exported and listed as operational.** Mode 2 still reads its live rows. Being operational only means its own differences are counted rather than explained (A1.9 rule 4). Nothing stops a rule from reading it as evidence.

### A3.2 Automation rows: options weighed and the rule

| Option | Verdict |
| --- | --- |
| (a) D-260 literally: explain a service row when `automation_execution.initiating_user_id` is a journalled actor | **Improved, not adopted alone.** It is correct where it applies, and it is kept as a cross-check. But it is NULL for every seeded starter (A3.1), which covers every measured row. |
| (b) Write `on_behalf_of_user_id` on the worker's events (DO-D3 Q2a option 1) | **Rejected.** It changes product attribution to fit a test. Starters run as the service identity by design (D-142 Q3; ADR-0044 §1). Saying "on behalf of" a user who did not ask for it would misstate the trail. It would also change 0074-era behaviour that DG5/DG6 approved. |

- **The outbox row is written in the transaction of the mutation that raised it.** Examples:
  - `createTransformation` writes aggregate `transformation` (`routes.ts` l.298);
  - `submitGate` and `decideGate` write aggregate `gate_instance` (`gates.ts` `enqueueGateEvent`).

  `outbox_event.created_at` and `audit_event.occurred_at` both default to `now()`, PostgreSQL's transaction timestamp. Neither insert path sets them (`packages/db/src/audit.ts`, `apps/api/src/modules/jobs/outbox.ts`, `gates.ts`). So the mutation's audit event and its outbox row carry the **same** timestamp.
- **The worker's own writes carry the job.** Every worker audit event has `request_id = 'job:<pg-boss job id>'` (`jobActor`). A starter wrapper and the handler it wraps run in the same job, so they write under the same `request_id`. The engine (queue `automation.evaluate`) writes its executions and their actions' effects in its own job, again under one `request_id`. That includes the execution, the action result and the handler's outputs, such as a gate routing's approval rows.
- **`outbox_event` is exported and listed as operational.** Mode 2 still reads its live rows. Being operational only means its own differences are counted rather than explained (A1.9 rule 4). Nothing stops a rule from reading it as evidence.

### A3.2 Automation rows: options weighed and the rule

| Option | Verdict |
| --- | --- |
| (a) D-260 literally: explain a service row when `automation_execution.initiating_user_id` is a journalled actor | **Improved, not adopted alone.** It is correct where it applies, and it is kept as a cross-check. But it is NULL for every seeded starter (A3.1), which covers every measured row. |
| (b) Write `on_behalf_of_user_id` on the worker's events (DO-D3 Q2a option 1) | **Rejected.** It changes product attribution to fit a test. Starters run as the service identity by design (D-142 Q3; ADR-0044 §1). Saying "on behalf of" a user who did not ask for it would misstate the trail. It would also change 0074-era behaviour that DG5/DG6 approved. |

cd /home/user/My-owns/docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG7/qa/round-5/a18 && cat > qa-r5-d9-boundary-repro.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# qa-verifier DG7 round 5 (T-DG7-REV-QA-R5): deliberate reproduction of the A18 D9 FAIL of run 1. Builds an archive from
# the FROZEN clone (02aeed6e, candidate 07af9fba), waits until $QA_START (UTC HH:MM:SS) so that the drill's D7-D9 window
# (target worker running) contains a quarter hour (approval.escalation_scan, */15 Asia/Riyadh), runs
# deploy/scripts/transfer-drill.sh --keep, then starts the kept TARGET PostgreSQL on a host port read-only-in-intent and
# SELECTs the automation_execution rows whose trigger is a schedule (trigger code, key, times). Nothing is changed in the
# product, the drill or the candidate; no job is paused or rescheduled. SYNTHETIC data only; nothing here approves
# anything (no G1-G6, Finance, IT or DG approval). Run under tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh.
set -u
REPO="${QA_REPO:?}"; OUT="${QA_OUT:?}"; START="${QA_START:?}"; B="$TMPDIR/qa-r5-d9"; CAND=sha256:07af9fba26f9ae435f6f3de7ca5204ed1e182a125f1fd0f912b70da06035a61d
[ -e "$B" ] && { echo "BLOCKED: $B exists"; exit 2; }
cd "$REPO"; ts() { date -u +%T; }
echo "start $(ts); HEAD $(git rev-parse HEAD); target drill start $START"
U=$(node -e 'const u=new URL(process.env.TEST_DATABASE_ADMIN_URL);u.pathname="/mth_d9_src";u.username="mth_owner";console.log(u.href)')
psql -X -q -d "$TEST_DATABASE_ADMIN_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 <<SQL
DO \$\$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname='mth_owner') THEN CREATE ROLE mth_owner LOGIN; END IF;
IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname='mth_app') THEN CREATE ROLE mth_app LOGIN; END IF; END \$\$;
CREATE DATABASE mth_d9_src OWNER mth_owner ENCODING 'UTF8' TEMPLATE template0;
GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE mth_d9_src TO mth_app;
SQL
(cd packages/db && DATABASE_OWNER_URL="$U" NODE_ENV=development node --conditions=@mth/source src/cli.ts migrate >/dev/null && \
  DATABASE_OWNER_URL="$U" NODE_ENV=development node --conditions=@mth/source src/cli.ts seed-demo | grep "reporting periods relative to") || { echo "demo db FAIL"; exit 1; }
DATABASE_OWNER_URL="$U" NODE_ENV=development node tools/migration/export.mjs --out "$B/export" --operator "transfer-drill synthetic operator" | tail -1
node tools/release/build-archive.mjs --repo "$REPO" --commit "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" --demo-data "$B/export" --candidate $CAND --out "$B/arch" | tail -1
A=$(ls "$B"/arch/*.tar.gz | head -1); S=$(sha256sum "$A" | cut -c1-64); echo "archive $(basename "$A") sha256 $S"
psql -X -q -d "$TEST_DATABASE_ADMIN_URL" -c "DROP DATABASE mth_d9_src WITH (FORCE);"; rm -rf "$B/export"
mkdir -p "$B/store" && cp -a "${QA_STORE_SRC:?}" "$B/store/v10"
now=$(date -u +%s); tgt=$(date -u -d "$START" +%s); [ "$tgt" -gt "$now" ] && { echo "waiting $((tgt-now)) s until $START"; sleep $((tgt-now)); }
mkdir -p "$OUT"; W="$B/work"
echo "--- transfer-drill.sh --keep start $(ts)"
bash deploy/scripts/transfer-drill.sh --archive "$A" --sha256 "$S" --store "$B/store" --out "$OUT" --work "$W" --keep > "$OUT/stdout.txt" 2> "$OUT/stderr.txt"
rc=$?; echo "drill exit $rc $(ts)"; grep -E '^transfer-drill: (step D[0-9]+ (start|PASS|FAIL)|PASS|FAIL)' "$OUT/stdout.txt" | cut -c1-160
grep -n "automation_" "$OUT/step-D9.log" 2>/dev/null
echo "--- kept target cluster: start on 127.0.0.1:32595 and read the schedule-triggered executions"
PGBIN=$(ls -d /usr/lib/postgresql/*/bin | sort -V | tail -1)
"$PGBIN/pg_ctl" -D "$W/pgT/data" -o "-p 32595 -k $W -c listen_addresses=127.0.0.1" -l "$B/pgT-host.log" -w start >/dev/null && echo "started"

pg_init() { # pg_init <dir> <port> <pidvar>
  local dir="$1" port="$2"
  mkdir -p "$dir" && chmod 0777 "$dir"
  rand >"$dir.su" && chmod 0644 "$dir.su"
  as_pg "$PGBIN/initdb" -D "$dir/data" -U postgres --pwfile="$dir.su" --auth-local=trust --auth-host=scram-sha-256 \
    --encoding=UTF8 --locale=C >/dev/null
}
pg_start() { # pg_start <dir> <port> -> echoes the pid
  local dir="$1" port="$2"
  # T-DG7-DO-D4 (T-B11 attempt 2, D1 after 31.7 s with an empty step log): `-k "$dir"` made the postmaster create a Unix
  # socket, which the host sandbox refuses ("could not create Unix socket ... Operation not permitted", then FATAL "could
  # not create any Unix-domain sockets"). Every connection of the drill is TCP on 127.0.0.1 (su_url), so no Unix socket
  # is created, as tests/qa/support/pg-port.sh does.
  as_pg "$PGBIN/postgres" -D "$dir/data" -p "$port" -c unix_socket_directories='' -c listen_addresses=127.0.0.1 \
    >>"$dir/pg.log" 2>&1 &
  local pid=$!
  for _ in $(seq 1 120); do
    PGPASSWORD="$(cat "$dir.su")" "$PGBIN/psql" -h 127.0.0.1 -p "$port" -U postgres -d postgres -qAtc 'select 1' \
      >/dev/null 2>&1 && { echo "$pid"; return 0; }
    sleep 0.25
  done
  echo "PostgreSQL on port $port did not accept connections within 30 s; $dir/pg.log ends:" >&2
  tail -5 "$dir/pg.log" >&2
  return 1
}
su_url() { printf 'postgres://postgres:%s@127.0.0.1:%s/%s' "$(cat "$1.su")" "$2" "${3:-postgres}"; }

# DG7 round 5: qa-verifier narrative

- **Task:** T-DG7-REV-QA-R5
- **Session:** f4c61bca-0439-49d8-b5b0-06f48cd84441
- **Candidate:** `sha256:07af9fba26f9ae435f6f3de7ca5204ed1e182a125f1fd0f912b70da06035a61d` (source `02aeed6e`, 3155 files)
- **Verdict: FAIL.** One new Medium finding, F-DG7-971 (A18 drill result depends on the wall clock). F-DG7-922, 941 and 970 are verified closed.

## What changed since round 4

The round-4 and round-5 manifests differ in one file, `docs/delivery/decisions.md`, which gained the D-277 row. `candidate.mjs --diff` ignores a path argument and always compares with the current stage manifest, so I compared the two manifests directly. Outside the candidate, only `stages.json`, `findings.json` and `progress.md` changed, plus the round-4 assignments, manifest and records. Product code, tests and handover texts are unchanged (`git diff 471072d6 02aeed6e` over apps, packages, deploy, tools, tests, e2e, licenses, scripts and docs/handover|architecture|api is empty).

## F-DG7-922 / 941 / 970 (stages.json transition): closed

The DG7 history is now legal and its timestamps increase strictly. Each round pairs with a REVIEWING entry, followed by FIXING once the round is finished. A revert-to-fail probe brings back `DG7 illegal transition REVIEWING -> REVIEWING`.

Validator results:

- `--historical` DG6…DG1, `--reconcile`, `--pipeline` and `--register DG7` all pass.
- `--stage DG7` reports only the missing gate record, which is expected before the release audit.

I accept the late-recorded entry:

- it is appended, not a history rewrite;
- its note says it was recorded late and why;
- its time is the real commit time of the round-3 findings import (5458273cd, 01:38:50Z);
- D-277 records the outcome.

## F-DG7-971 (new, Medium): A18 D9 fails on a quarter hour

**What I saw.** In my first A18 run the direct drill passed. The shipped harness on the same archive then failed 4 of 10 tests. Its D9 restart landed just after 07:15Z, and the mode 2 recheck found one unexplained `automation_execution` and its `automation_action_result`. Only that run's worker ran `approval.escalation_scan` after the restart.

**Cause.** That queue is the schedule-triggered starter `starter.decision_sla` (`*/15`, Asia/Riyadh). ADR-0064 A3.9 residual 1 keeps schedule-triggered rows unexplained by design and says "the orchestrator decides". No decision was ever recorded, because DO-D4 never hit the case.

**Reproduction.** I reproduced it on demand on the unmodified candidate by timing `transfer-drill.sh --keep` across 08:00Z. D9 failed. The kept target database holds exactly the one execution, with key `approval.escalation_scan:2026-11-16T08:00`, plus its starter result. The other runs passed: the harness re-run at 07:20, and a reproduction attempt that missed 07:45 by 3 s.

**Effect.**

- The A18 acceptance drill gives FAIL on about 5–7 % of runs, on time of day alone.
- The product's records, jobs and approvals are correct in every run.
- The residual is not disclosed in `known-limitations.md`, the release notes, `deployment.md`, or the A18 register rows.

**Severity.** Medium per D-192: a real, bounded defect in the acceptance drill. It is not mandatory, because no data or access is wrong. The owner is solution-architect, because the decision belongs to A3.9. The ADR forbids pausing or rescheduling the job to dodge it.

## Product checks re-run on this candidate (all in a disposable shared clone at 02aeed6e)

**Static checks.** Build, typecheck, lint, openapi-lint, no-cdn and prettier all exit 0.

**Unit.** The first attempt hit EROFS: Vite writes into `node_modules/.vite-temp`, and I had symlinked a read-only `node_modules`. I fixed this with a writable shim and re-ran. Results:

- unit-node 3036/3036 plus one file re-run 6/6. That file had failed with ENOENT because my sparse clone first omitted `docs/delivery/handbacks`; I restored them.
- unit-web 2199/2199.
- nocodegen 259 passed, 2 skipped by design.

**Other suites:**

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| Integration | 475 files; 4696 passed, 8 skipped, 1 todo (same as round 4) |
| Tool suites | 66 / 39 / 29 / 189 / 466 (464 passed + 2 explained skips) |
| Release tools and check-handover | PASS |
| Protocol audit | Same counts as round 4: C2 27, C3 7, C5 1 |
| A19 restore drill | R1–R9 PASS |
| Offline drill | 10/10 specs, 293 connection-log lines, all loopback |
| Root acceptance | 288 passed, 18 designed axe skips; connection log loopback only |
| Product e2e | en 286 passed + 1 skipped; ar and keyboard as recorded in the JSON |
| A27 K11 | Re-drill at 02aeed6e PASS |

I could not reach the Docker daemon (permission denied). The container half is judged on the orchestrator's host-run 3b/3c evidence, whose server surface is unchanged since then; I did not run it myself.

## Assignment note

The assignment asks for `round: 7`. The validator (`rules.mjs` l.682 and l.794) requires the record's `round` to equal the round directory, here 5, so I wrote `round: 5`. I did not raise this as a finding: the assignment is write-once and the validator enforces the right value.
